additional_concerns: Footnote 3 is supplied in da12aecad4e68.u30.3569. Both extracted permissions retain stale statements that it is missing. It requires a Hongkong Post e-Cert for the marked XML and PDF options; the web-form option has no such marker.
The XML permission is supported subject to the schema and e-Cert requirements. Its listed conditions omit e-Cert and should not be treated as an exhaustive statement of compliance.
The four external dependency IDs have null source_hash values and no descriptions mapping them to particular authorities. None can be classified AVAILABLE or confidently assigned to the XML schema.

The compliance candidates expressly exclude XML-schema conformity from their XML facts. This is consistent with a narrowly selected channel, method and e-Cert control, but TRUE must not be presented as full XML-submission compliance. The separate technical-test arrangement is also outside these formulas.

The circular does not specify how an e-Cert must be supplied or used. The compliance candidates appropriately defer that assessment, but any operational interpretation needs additional JFIU authority; possession alone and a particular attachment or signing procedure are not established by the supplied sentence.

node.5d8c4ca625a46c41ff2f4098 uses a calendar-date threshold that includes the pre-9:00am blackout on 2 February. The other candidates use operational launch. Retain the date-effect and operational-launch interpretations pending resolution; they are not equivalent.
The governing timezone is not expressly stated in the supplied text. An authoritative timezone basis is missing for absolute event-time comparisons.
Some event candidates classify a non-filing as OUT_OF_SCOPE, whereas node.29b224046d115582fbf223fb can return FALSE. Clarify the assessment domain before treating those outputs as equivalent.
The report-history candidate answers whether a triggering event ever existed. A later resubmission does not erase that historical fact; TRUE does not establish that a duty remains outstanding.
The migration passage describes access to historical records, not a new submission or satisfaction of a submission control. Its absence from these compliance formulas is not a defect.
